claims.title: Founding of the Sukhothai kingdom
claims.summary: Tai chiefs cast off Khmer rule and establish Sukhothai in the upper Chao Phraya valley, traditionally counted as the first independent Thai kingdom.

sources.label: Historic Town of Sukhothai and Associated Historic Towns

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Thailand: The only Southeast Asian land never colonised — a kingdom that bent so as not to break.", terralore.co/country/THA/chronicle#ev-1238-founding-of-the-sukhothai-kingdom, claim TL:THA:event:1238:founding-of-the-sukhothai-kingdom, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Creation of the Thai script
claims.summary: King Ramkhamhaeng is traditionally credited with devising the Thai alphabet, recorded on a stone inscription dated 1292, the earliest known text in the Thai language.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Thailand: The only Southeast Asian land never colonised — a kingdom that bent so as not to break.", terralore.co/country/THA/chronicle#ev-1283-creation-of-the-thai-script, claim TL:THA:event:1283:creation-of-the-thai-script, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Reign of Ramkhamhaeng the Great
claims.summary: Sukhothai reaches its zenith under Ramkhamhaeng, who expands its reach, opens relations with China, and champions Theravada Buddhism.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Thailand: The only Southeast Asian land never colonised — a kingdom that bent so as not to break.", terralore.co/country/THA/chronicle#ev-1279-reign-of-ramkhamhaeng-the-great, claim TL:THA:event:1279:reign-of-ramkhamhaeng-the-great, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Sukhothai absorbed by Ayutthaya
claims.summary: After a century of decline, Sukhothai is reduced to a vassal and finally incorporated into the expanding kingdom of Ayutthaya.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Thailand: The only Southeast Asian land never colonised — a kingdom that bent so as not to break.", terralore.co/country/THA/chronicle#ev-1438-sukhothai-absorbed-by-ayutthaya, claim TL:THA:event:1438:sukhothai-absorbed-by-ayutthaya, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Foundation of Ayutthaya
claims.summary: King Ramathibodi I founds Ayutthaya at the meeting of three rivers, beginning a kingdom that would dominate the Chao Phraya basin for over four centuries.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Thailand: The only Southeast Asian land never colonised — a kingdom that bent so as not to break.", terralore.co/country/THA/chronicle#ev-1351-foundation-of-ayutthaya, claim TL:THA:event:1351:foundation-of-ayutthaya, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: First Burmese conquest of Ayutthaya
claims.summary: Burmese forces capture Ayutthaya and reduce it to vassalage; the kingdom later recovers its full independence under King Naresuan.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Thailand: The only Southeast Asian land never colonised — a kingdom that bent so as not to break.", terralore.co/country/THA/chronicle#ev-1569-first-burmese-conquest-of-ayutthaya, claim TL:THA:event:1569:first-burmese-conquest-of-ayutthaya, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Reign of King Narai and the French embassies
claims.summary: Under Narai, Ayutthaya reaches a height of international contact, exchanging embassies with Louis XIV's France and welcoming traders from across Eurasia.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Thailand: The only Southeast Asian land never colonised — a kingdom that bent so as not to break.", terralore.co/country/THA/chronicle#ev-1656-reign-of-king-narai-and-the-french-embassies, claim TL:THA:event:1656:reign-of-king-narai-and-the-french-embassies, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Sack of Ayutthaya by Burma
claims.summary: A Burmese army storms and burns Ayutthaya after a prolonged siege, ending the kingdom and leaving the celebrated city in ruins.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Thailand: The only Southeast Asian land never colonised — a kingdom that bent so as not to break.", terralore.co/country/THA/chronicle#ev-1767-sack-of-ayutthaya-by-burma, claim TL:THA:event:1767:sack-of-ayutthaya-by-burma, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Taksin establishes Thonburi
claims.summary: Taksin rallies resistance after the fall of Ayutthaya, drives out the Burmese, and founds a new capital at Thonburi, where he is crowned king.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Thailand: The only Southeast Asian land never colonised — a kingdom that bent so as not to break.", terralore.co/country/THA/chronicle#ev-1767-taksin-establishes-thonburi, claim TL:THA:event:1767:taksin-establishes-thonburi, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Founding of the Chakri dynasty and Bangkok
claims.summary: After Taksin's fall, the general Chao Phraya Chakri takes the throne as Rama I, founds the Chakri dynasty, and establishes the new capital of Bangkok.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Thailand: The only Southeast Asian land never colonised — a kingdom that bent so as not to break.", terralore.co/country/THA/chronicle#ev-1782-founding-of-the-chakri-dynasty-and-bangkok, claim TL:THA:event:1782:founding-of-the-chakri-dynasty-and-bangkok, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Reign of Rama I
claims.summary: Rama I rebuilds the Siamese state, revising its laws and Buddhist scriptures and restoring its power over neighbouring vassal states.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Thailand: The only Southeast Asian land never colonised — a kingdom that bent so as not to break.", terralore.co/country/THA/chronicle#ev-1782-reign-of-rama-i, claim TL:THA:event:1782:reign-of-rama-i, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The Bowring Treaty
claims.summary: King Mongkut signs the Bowring Treaty with Britain, opening Siam to Western trade and granting extraterritoriality; comparable treaties with other powers follow.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Thailand: The only Southeast Asian land never colonised — a kingdom that bent so as not to break.", terralore.co/country/THA/chronicle#ev-1855-the-bowring-treaty, claim TL:THA:event:1855:the-bowring-treaty, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Reforms of Chulalongkorn (Rama V)
claims.summary: Chulalongkorn abolishes slavery, reorganises the administration, and modernises law, finance, education, and infrastructure, building a centralised modern state.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Thailand: The only Southeast Asian land never colonised — a kingdom that bent so as not to break.", terralore.co/country/THA/chronicle#ev-1868-reforms-of-chulalongkorn-rama-v, claim TL:THA:event:1868:reforms-of-chulalongkorn-rama-v, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Franco-Siamese crisis and loss of Laos
claims.summary: After French gunboats threaten Bangkok, Siam cedes the Lao territories east of the Mekong to French Indochina, the heaviest of its frontier concessions.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Thailand: The only Southeast Asian land never colonised — a kingdom that bent so as not to break.", terralore.co/country/THA/chronicle#ev-1893-franco-siamese-crisis-and-loss-of-laos, claim TL:THA:event:1893:franco-siamese-crisis-and-loss-of-laos, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Anglo-French guarantee of Siam's independence
claims.summary: Britain and France declare their mutual respect for the independence of Siam's core territory, fixing the kingdom as a buffer state between their empires.

sources.label: The Anglo-French Declaration of January 1896 and the Independence of Siam
sources.publisher: The Siam Society (Journal of the Siam Society)

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Thailand: The only Southeast Asian land never colonised — a kingdom that bent so as not to break.", terralore.co/country/THA/chronicle#ev-1896-anglo-french-guarantee-of-siam-s-independence, claim TL:THA:event:1896:anglo-french-guarantee-of-siam-s-independence, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Constitutional revolution
claims.summary: The People's Party stages a bloodless coup forcing King Prajadhipok to accept a constitution, ending the absolute monarchy and creating a constitutional one.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Thailand: The only Southeast Asian land never colonised — a kingdom that bent so as not to break.", terralore.co/country/THA/chronicle#ev-1932-constitutional-revolution, claim TL:THA:event:1932:constitutional-revolution, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Siam renamed Thailand
claims.summary: The nationalist government of Phibun changes the country's name from Siam to Thailand, asserting a Tai national identity.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Thailand: The only Southeast Asian land never colonised — a kingdom that bent so as not to break.", terralore.co/country/THA/chronicle#ev-1939-siam-renamed-thailand, claim TL:THA:event:1939:siam-renamed-thailand, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Alliance with Japan in World War II
claims.summary: Phibun's government allies Thailand with Japan and declares war on Britain and the United States, while the Free Thai movement under Pridi resists covertly.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Thailand: The only Southeast Asian land never colonised — a kingdom that bent so as not to break.", terralore.co/country/THA/chronicle#ev-1942-alliance-with-japan-in-world-war-ii, claim TL:THA:event:1942:alliance-with-japan-in-world-war-ii, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Death of King Ananda and accession of Bhumibol
claims.summary: King Ananda Mahidol (Rama VIII) dies of a gunshot in unexplained circumstances and is succeeded by his brother Bhumibol Adulyadej (Rama IX).
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Thailand: The only Southeast Asian land never colonised — a kingdom that bent so as not to break.", terralore.co/country/THA/chronicle#ev-1946-death-of-king-ananda-and-accession-of-bhumibol, claim TL:THA:event:1946:death-of-king-ananda-and-accession-of-bhumibol, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Student uprising ends military rule
claims.summary: A mass student-led uprising, with royal intervention by King Bhumibol, forces the ruling generals from power and briefly opens a democratic interlude.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Thailand: The only Southeast Asian land never colonised — a kingdom that bent so as not to break.", terralore.co/country/THA/chronicle#ev-1973-student-uprising-ends-military-rule, claim TL:THA:event:1973:student-uprising-ends-military-rule, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Coup against Thaksin Shinawatra
claims.summary: The military ousts populist Prime Minister Thaksin Shinawatra while he is abroad, opening nearly two decades of conflict between his movement and the establishment.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Thailand: The only Southeast Asian land never colonised — a kingdom that bent so as not to break.", terralore.co/country/THA/chronicle#ev-2006-coup-against-thaksin-shinawatra, claim TL:THA:event:2006:coup-against-thaksin-shinawatra, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Coup against Yingluck Shinawatra
claims.summary: The army overthrows the government of Yingluck Shinawatra, ruling directly and later entrenching its role in a new constitution adopted in 2017.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Thailand: The only Southeast Asian land never colonised — a kingdom that bent so as not to break.", terralore.co/country/THA/chronicle#ev-2014-coup-against-yingluck-shinawatra, claim TL:THA:event:2014:coup-against-yingluck-shinawatra, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Death of Bhumibol; accession of Vajiralongkorn
claims.summary: King Bhumibol Adulyadej dies after a 70-year reign and is succeeded by his son Maha Vajiralongkorn (Rama X), who formally accepts the throne in December 2016.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Thailand: The only Southeast Asian land never colonised — a kingdom that bent so as not to break.", terralore.co/country/THA/chronicle#ev-2016-death-of-bhumibol-accession-of-vajiralongkorn, claim TL:THA:event:2016:death-of-bhumibol-accession-of-vajiralongkorn, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.
